Overview of the B2 First for Schools Reading and Use of English Paper

Aims of the lesson  To familiarise the students with the content of the First for Schools
                    Reading and Use of English paper (Paper 1)
Time needed
Materials required  35 minutes

                     Sample Reading and Use of English Paper (one copy for each 2–3
                         students)

                     Classroom Handout 1 (one per student)
                     Answer sheets (one copy for each small group of students)
                     http://www.cambridgeenglish.org/exams-and- qualifications/first-for-

                         schools/exam-update-for-2015/

Procedure

1. Before the class, stick up a copy of different tasks from the Sample Reading and Use of English
     Paper around the walls of the classroom. Samples can be found in the B2 First for Schools
     handbook.

2. Introduce the testing focus of the Reading and Use of English paper by asking students to call out if
     the following language areas come into knowledge of grammar or of vocabulary.

• verb tenses                            • suffixes
• phrasal verbs                          • prepositions
• collocation (words which go together)  • auxiliaries

• set phrases (e.g. See you later!)      • linkers

Do this quickly, just to get students thinking about language systems. You could point out that some
areas can fall under both grammar and vocabulary. Indeed many teachers and students see
grammar – vocabulary as a continuum rather than an either/or choice so it is perfectly fine for there
to be some ambiguity.
Timing: 5 mins

  3. Explain to students that the Reading and Use of English paper in B2 First for Schools tests their
      knowledge of these areas, and they are going to find out about it now. They aren’t going to do
      the tasks. Instead, they will answer some questions about the paper to find out what they have to
      do.
     Timing: 2 mins

  4. Give out Classroom handout 1, and say that if any students already know (or think they
      know) some of the answers, they can start to fill in the worksheet in pairs (or groups of 3).
      Timing: 5 mins

  5. Ask the students to go and look at the different tasks on the walls, and fill in as much missing
      information on their handout as possible in five minutes. Be strict about the timing. You could add a
      competitive element (who can get the most correct answers).
      Timing: 5 mins

6. Students count how many answers they’ve got. The student with the most
          answers reads theirs out. Encourage other students to correct any mistakes and to complete
          their own worksheets. Collect any missing answers from other students until the worksheet is
          complete (see Answe rs to Classroom handout 1).
          Timing: 5 mins

     7. Invite students to ask any other questions they may have about the Reading and Use of
          English paper. Discuss the following questions with students:
          Which part do you think you’ll find easiest? Which part do you think
          will be the most difficult?
          What aspect(s) do you think you’ll need to work on most? Vocabulary, grammar, spelling,
          reading skills, etc.
          Refer to the B2 First for Schools Handbook if necessary.
          Timing: 7 mins

          An alternative here if the students have had some practice would be to have them rank
          the activities in terms of difficulty and compare with a partner.

     8. Give out the answer sheets to each small group, so they can see where they will write their
          answers. Point out that they can write their answers on the question paper, but they must
          transfer their answers onto the answer sheet within the 1 hour 15 minutes. They have to
          shade in a small box in pencil or write a word or words in capital letters (they must not use
          pen to complete the answer sheet).
